labels.label: (no ETT label) ladder witness Causal.galileoCurve_separates
labels.notes: The model is the target's, field by field. lt = galileoCurveLt n: some γ : ℝ → ℝ × (Fin n → ℝ), ContinuousOn on [0,1], γ 0 = p, γ 1 = q, MapsTo [0,1] into U, time StrictMonoOn [0,1]. le U p q = galileoCurveLt n U p q ∨ (p = q ∧ p ∈ U). Both checked by Iff.rfl in the audit probe. It is a Causality (the library structure; the kernel checks every field). The I^± openness argument (isOpen_galileoGraphLt_right/_left) is correct: for y ∈ I⁺_U(x), take a ball B(y,ε) ⊆ U and a graph point w = (t₀, f t₀) with x.1 < t₀ < y.1 and w ∈ B(y,ε/2). On B(y,ε/2) ∩ {t₀ < z.1}, the segment from w to z stays in B(y,ε/2) ⊆ U, so x ≪ w ≪ z by concatenation. All 23 conjuncts elaborate against the ladder's own Lean names written in full in a probe: Causal.Causality.{CausallyArcConnected, PushUp, LocallyPushUp, CausallyOpen, CausallyOpenFuture, LocallyCausallyOpen, LocallyCausallyOpenFuture, Tarentin, ChronalNeighbours, HasChronalNeighbourEverywhere, CausallyPlain, IsCausal, HasTimeFunction, IsTimeFunction, FutureOneConnected, CurvesExtend, LocallyStronglyCausal, StronglyCausal, StronglyCausalOpen, CausallyCompact, GloballyHyperbolic} and Causal.Precausality.{AbsolutelyMinimal, AbsolutelyMinimalOn}. Together they cover the 21 causality-sort properties of programme/ladder.toml. Absolute minimality appears twice: the global AbsolutelyMinimal and ∀ W, AbsolutelyMinimalOn W (conjunct 3). It therefore holds in either reading of DEC-167. The negative conjuncts are genuine. ¬LocallyStronglyCausal comes from galileoCurve_not_stronglyCausalOn, which is non-vacuous: the probe instantiates n = 1, W = ⊤. It is correct against DiamondConfinement's StronglyCausalOn (∀ p ∈ W, ∀ U ∈ 𝓝 p, ∃ V ∈ 𝓝 p, V ⊆ U ∧ CausallyConvexIn V W, checked by Iff.rfl). The argument: take U = {x₁}ᶜ, with x₁ the point of a ball B ⊆ W beside p at the same time (x₁ ≠ p since n ≥ 1). V holds a ∈ B before p and b ∈ B after p, and a ≪_W x₁ ≪_W b by straight segments in B. So x₁ ∈ J_W(a,b) ⊆ V ⊆ {x₁}ᶜ, a contradiction. ¬CausallyCompact: J((0,0),(2,0)) holds (1, B+1, …) for every B. ¬SC, ¬SCO and ¬GH follow from ¬LSC and ¬CC through the ladder edges strongly_causal ⇒ LSC, SCO ⇒ SC and GH ⇒ CC. The 16 positive conjuncts are the target's list plus their local and one-sided forms. The docstring marks no label: the ledger's mark regex needs `prefix:`, and **`Causal.galileoCurve_separates`** is a Lean name.

findings.what: The OQ-108 account is right in substance but imprecise in two places that matter if it becomes an addendum. (i) It calls Precausality.generated 'the library's sense' of generation. Precausality.generated formalizes the paper's own def:precausality_generated_notation_lemma (ETT.tex:393, through lem:union_causalite, ETT.tex:367), the notion def:topological_space_causality_absolutely (ETT.tex:398) is phrased in. The ambiguity is therefore between the paper's own generation over a cover and chains of printed relations in convex opens; it is not between the library and the paper. (ii) It says generation over a cover gives 'a different causality'. By lem:union_causalite, generated(S, printed) equals the printed relation on every open inside a member of S. The same bounded, scaled cup inside one member, with the scaled cover {t > 1/4}, {t < 1/2}, then shows (argued) that it is not absolutely minimal. It is also cover-dependent. Under DEC-167 it is no causality at all, not 'a different causality'.
findings.fix: In the REPORT question, and in SCOPE if desired, write: 'with the paper's own generation (def:precausality_generated_notation_lemma, Precausality.generated) over any fixed cover, the result agrees with the printed relation inside each member. It is a different precausality, depends on the cover and is (argued) not absolutely minimal, so it is no causality under DEC-167'. A formulation that avoids the word 'generate' may help the author (auditor's argument, not in Lean). The curve form is the greatest precausality below the printed one that is absolutely minimal on every open set. Proof: let Q ≤ printed be hereditarily absolutely minimal and Q ≪_V p q. Apply AbsolutelyMinimalOn V to the cover of V by the balls inside V. Each step is Q ≪_B ⊆ printed ≪_B = curve ≪_B, B convex (galileoCurve_lt_iff_galileo_of_convex). Then mono and transitivity give curve ≪_V p q; the same works for ≤. It would take a few lines in Lean.
